My team and I just shipped our first build for the @BNBChain Tokenized Stocks Hackathon.

Meet First Share.

We’re building a simple way for anyone to understand and access tokenized US stocks, even if they’re completely new to crypto or investing.

Imagine being able to buy your first $5 worth of a tokenized stock like Tesla or NVIDIA on BNB Chain without feeling lost.

That’s the idea behind First Share.

Before you spend a cent, we explain the important things needed to be known:

→ Is the stock backed?
→ Is the market open?
→ Is the price fair?
→ What should you know before buying?

Because onboarding people into tokenized stocks shouldn't require them to understand everything about crypto first.

I believe tokenized stocks could become a huge part of this industry, and we want to build something that makes getting started easier for everyone.

We’re currently on testnet, and this is only our first build. There’s still a lot to improve, and we’re committed to making First Share better.

We also see an opportunity to bring this into the @vibevibefun ecosystem, where stock-related products are already part of the conversation.

We’re vibecoding, learning, shipping, and improving as we go.

The goal isn't just to build another hackathon project. It's to make tokenized stocks easier for people to understand and access.

We're open to feedback, ideas, and people who want to help us build this into something bigger. 🫡

Dear Chuma,

Thank you for your feedback. Actually, plantation overseers tended to be Europeans, usually Scottish (for the British), and fellow Portuguese in Brazil. For example, Bob Marley's father was a plantation overseer, although slavery had ended by then. 

According to official Brazilian government records, the majority of the enslaved people in Brazil who were shipped from West Africa were taken from Badagry. Chuma, it was almost exclusively Lukumi Yoruba enslaved people that were sold at Badagry. 

Igbo enslaved people (then known as Eboe) were shipped from Bonny (sold by the Ijaws), Koko (sold by the Itsekiri), and Ughoton (sold by the Binis).

But, let us, for the sake of argument, say that you are right, and that most of the Black people in Brazil are of Igbo descent, and they only adopted Lukumi Yoruba culture; it is still a thing of pride for the Nigerian nation. 

Igbos are a credit to Nigeria and the world and always rise to the top wherever they find themselves, and Nigeria is proud of these much-loved people. 

Thanks again, Chuma, and may God bless you
